newsitem.title: DUBAI: Mideast Gulf oil outlook - all eyes on Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Mideast Gulf oil outlook - all eyes on Iraq.

text.p: The middle distillates market in the Middle East Gulf is waiting to see if demand for jet kerosene, already in short supply, is boosted further following the U.S. missile attacks on Iraq, Gulf traders said on Thursday.
"Everyone is watching out for missiles. There is not much else going on in middle distillates," said one.
"It is very wait-and-see at the moment due to what's going on in Iraq," said another trader.
"With all the flying going on we will probably see demand for jet. Jet has been quite long, but it is steady now," he added.

The United States fired 44 cruise missiles from bombers and warships in the Gulf to air-defence targets in southern Iraq on Tuesday and Wednesday in response to Iraq's military involvement in Kurdish factional fighting in the north of the country.
"It depends on how long it (the attacks) goes on for. If the crisis goes on for a month, then we'll see premiums higher," said a trader.
President Bill Clinton said the United States had achieved the goals it set itself following Iraq's military incursion into the north but he did not rule out further attacks.
Jet kerosene was assessed at $28.40-28.80 a barrel fob Gulf on Thursday from $27.40-27.70 a week earlier. Premiums were seen higher, at between 80 cents and a dollar.
Traders said they were awaiting the outcome of Indian tenders for October: "We're waiting to see the Indian kero jet tender award."
The state-owned Indian Oil Corp has invited tenders for 90,000 tonne cargoes to Madras or Haldia and 30,000 tonne cargoes to Bombay for October delivery. The tenders close on Thursday.
Gas oil premiums were seen stronger than those on jet at around $1. Gas oil, assessed at $25.50-25.70 a barrel fob Gulf, was up from the previous week's $24.00-$24.20.
Traders see the market remaining tight in the next few weeks, with some surplus arising closer to October.
Market players are also pinning their hopes on higher demand from India.
